newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Claudette pushes north.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Claudette pushes north.

text.p: Residents of the U.S. mid-Atlantic states were cautioned on Monday to watch the progress of Tropical Storm Claudette as it crept northward in the Atlantic Ocean.
Forecasters at the National Hurricane Center said the storm was not a large threat to the U.S. mainland but its future track was uncertain.
At 5 a.m. EDT (0900 GMT), Claudette was located at latitude 32.8 north, longitude 72.8 west, about 230 miles (370 km) southeast of Cape Hatteras, North Carolina, with winds of 45 mph (72 kph).
It was moving north at about 5 mph (8 kph) and was expected to turn gradually toward the north-northeast during the next 24 hours, forecasters said.
Claudette, the third named storm of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season, formed Sunday.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when sustained winds reach 39 mph (62 kph). Tropical storms become hurricanes when winds hit 74 mph (118 kph).
